hook.convey: closed shape → walk its edge from one corner, along every side, back to that same corner → the distance walked = perimeter; a rectangular cricket pitch, the border of a drawing sheet, a fence along a garden bed

use.hi: Cricket ki pitch socho, lagbhag 20 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi. Ek kone se chalo, kinaare-kinaare pitch ghoomkar wahin lauto. Jitna chale, utna pitch ka parimap hai. Yahi chakkar ab ek triangle par.
use.en: Think of a cricket pitch, about 20 m long and 3 m wide. Start at a corner and walk round its edge back to the same spot. However far you walked is the pitch's perimeter. Now the same walk round a triangle.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ke chaaron taraf colour se border banate ho na. Woh poori border jitni lambi hai, utna hi sheet ka parimap hai. Ab yahi border ek chhote triangle par dekhte hain.
use.en: You know the coloured border you draw all round a drawing sheet. However long that whole border is, that is the sheet's perimeter. Now let's see the same border on a small triangle.

use.hi: Garden mein phoolon ki kyari ke chaaron taraf baad lagti hai. Har bhuja par lagti hai. Ek bhi chhoot gayi, toh bakri seedha andar. Ab ek chhote triangle ke kinaare par yahi dekhte hain.
use.en: In a garden, a fence goes all round a flower bed. It goes on every side. Miss even one, and a goat walks straight in. Now let's see this on the edge of a small triangle.

explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary of a closed shape → start at a corner, go along every side, end back at that corner; triangle 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm → all three sides go into the sum

viewCaption.hi: Triangle ki teeno bhujayein khol ke ek seedhi line par rakhi hain: 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm, ek ke baad ek. Ungli ka poora safar yahi line hai.
viewCaption.en: The triangle's three sides are opened out onto one straight line: 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm, one after another. This line is your finger's whole trip.

prompt.hi: Parimap mein kitni bhujaon ki lambai aati hai, do ki ya teeno ki?
prompt.en: How many sides' lengths go into the perimeter, two or all three?

say.hi: Parimap mein teeno bhujaon ki lambai aati hai.
say.en: The perimeter takes the lengths of all three sides.

point.hi: Is triangle ki teen bhujayein hain, 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm. Ek kone par ungli rakho aur kinaare par chalao: pehli bhuja, doosri, teesri, aur wapas usi kone par. Ungli jitna chali, wahi parimap hai.
point.en: This triangle has three sides, 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. Put a finger on one corner and run it along the edge: first side, second, third, and back to the same corner. However far your finger went, that is the perimeter.

pointAlt.hi: Socho is triangle ka kinaara ek dhaage se bana hai. Ek kone se dhaaga khol ke seedha kar do: 4 cm, phir 5 cm, phir 6 cm, sab ek line mein. Us seedhi line ki poori lambai hi parimap hai.
pointAlt.en: Picture this triangle's edge made of a thread. Open the thread at one corner and lay it straight: 4 cm, then 5 cm, then 6 cm, all in one line. The whole length of that straight line is the perimeter.

prompt.hi: Ungli kone se chal ke wapas usi kone tak kul kitne cm chali?
prompt.en: How many cm in all did your finger go, from the corner back to that same corner?

reask.hi: Is triangle ki bhujayein 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm hain; iska parimap kitna hai?
reask.en: This triangle's sides are 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm; what is its perimeter?

did.hi: triangle ke kinaare par chalkar uski poori lambai nikali
did.en: went along a triangle's edge and found its whole length

why.hi: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 cm, teeno bhujayein judi, koi nahi chhooti
why.en: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 cm: all three sides in, none missed

whyAlt.hi: 4 aur 5 se 9 hua, aur 9 mein 6 aur jodo toh 15 cm; 6 chhod dete toh sirf 9 cm, yaani kinaara adhoora.
whyAlt.en: 4 and 5 make 9, and 6 more on 9 makes 15 cm; leave out the 6 and it is only 9 cm, an unfinished edge.

simpler.hi: Board ki line dekho: ungli ka poora safar wahi hai. Us line ki har bhuja ki lambai milakar socho.
simpler.en: Look at the line on the board: that is the finger's whole trip. Think of the lengths of every side on that line put together.

simpler.hi: Kinaara matlab shape ki bahar wali line. Ungli ek kone se chal ke har bhuja se guzarti hai, aur jis kone se chali thi wahin rukti hai.
simpler.en: The edge is the shape's outside line. A finger starting at a corner passes along every side and stops at the corner it started from.

explain.convey: any polygon (bahubhuj) → same rule: add every side, however many; hexagon = 6 sides → 6 lengths in the sum; regular hexagon with only one side labelled 5 cm → the unlabelled sides still belong to the boundary → still added

viewCaption.hi: Hexagon ki chhahon bhujayein ek line par lagi hain, har bhuja 5 cm ki. Jin bhujaon par label nahi tha, woh bhi is line mein hain.
viewCaption.en: All six sides of the hexagon sit on one line, each side 5 cm. The sides that had no label are on this line too.

prompt.hi: Hexagon ki kitni bhujaon par label likha hai?
prompt.en: On how many of the hexagon's sides is a label written?

say.hi: Label sirf ek bhuja par likha hai.
say.en: The label is written on only one side.

point.hi: Yeh hexagon hai, chhah bhujaon wala. Sab bhujayein barabar hain, par label sirf ek par hai: 5 cm. Baaki par kuch likha nahi, phir bhi woh kinaare mein aati hain. Parimap mein har bhuja aati hai, likhi ho ya na ho.
point.en: This is a hexagon, a shape with six sides. All its sides are equal, but only one has a label: 5 cm. Nothing is written on the others, yet they are still part of the edge. Every side goes into the perimeter, labelled or not.

pointAlt.hi: Shahad ke chhatte ka ek khaana dekho: uski chhah bhujayein hoti hain, sab ek jaisi. Yahan ek bhuja par 5 cm likha hai, toh baaki paanch bhi 5 cm ki hain. Parimap ke liye chhahon bhujayein ginni hain, sirf likhi hui nahi.
pointAlt.en: Look at one cell of a honeycomb: it has six sides, all alike. Here one side says 5 cm, so the other five are 5 cm too. For the perimeter we count all six sides, not just the labelled one.

prompt.hi: Poore hexagon ka parimap kitna hua?
prompt.en: What is the perimeter of the whole hexagon?

did.hi: hexagon ki bina label wali bhujayein bhi parimap mein gini
did.en: counted a hexagon's unlabelled sides in its perimeter too

why.hi: chhah bhujayein, har ek 5 cm ki: 6 × 5 = 30 cm
why.en: six sides of 5 cm each: 6 × 5 = 30 cm

whyAlt.hi: 5 cm ko ek-ek karke chhah baar jodo: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, toh 30 cm.
whyAlt.en: Add 5 cm six times, one by one: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, so 30 cm.

simpler.hi: Ungli ko hexagon ke kinaare par ek poora chakkar ghumao, aur har bhuja par uski lambai jodte jao.
simpler.en: Take your finger once all round the hexagon's edge, adding each side's length as you go.

simpler.hi: Likhi hui bhuja ke saath wali bhuja dekho: woh bhi utni hi lambi hai, aur uske aage wali bhi. Hexagon ka kinaara aisi hi bhujaon se poora banta hai.
simpler.en: Look at the side next to the labelled one: it is just as long, and so is the one after it. The hexagon's whole edge is made of sides like these.

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND the shape (a thread along the edge) → a length → cm, m, km; area (kshetrafal) = INSIDE (tiles covering the surface) → a different quantity; 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle → the edge goes 6, 4, 6, 4 → add them, never 6 × 4

viewCaption.hi: Rectangle ka kinaara ek dhaage ki tarah khul gaya hai: 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm. Andar ki jagah is line mein nahi aati.
viewCaption.en: The rectangle's edge has opened out like a thread: 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm. The space inside is not part of this line.

prompt.hi: Dhaaga kahan chalta hai, kinaare par ya andar?
prompt.en: Where does the thread run, on the edge or inside?

say.en: The thread runs on the edge.

point.hi: Ab yeh rectangle dekho, 6 cm lamba aur 4 cm chauda. Parimap ek dhaaga hai jo kinaare par chalta hai: pehle 6, phir bagal ki bhuja 4, phir 6, phir 4. Andar ki jagah area hai, woh bilkul alag cheez hai.
point.en: Now look at this rectangle, 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. The perimeter is a thread running along the edge: first 6, then 4 down the side, then 6, then 4. The space inside is the area, a completely different thing.

pointAlt.hi: Is rectangle ko ek photo frame socho. Frame ki lakdi sirf kinaare par hoti hai, 6, 4, 6 aur 4; beech mein photo hoti hai. Lakdi ki poori lambai parimap hai, aur photo ki jagah area.
pointAlt.en: Think of this rectangle as a photo frame. The wood is only on the edge, 6, 4, 6 and 4; the photo sits in the middle. The wood's whole length is the perimeter, and the photo's space is the area.

prompt.hi: Kinaare par ek baar dhaaga lapetna hai. Kitna dhaaga lagega?
prompt.en: We wrap a thread once round the edge. How much thread do we need?

reask.hi: 6 cm lambe, 4 cm chaude rectangle ke kinaare par ek baar lapetne mein kitna dhaaga lagega?
reask.en: How much thread goes once round the edge of a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide?

did.hi: andar ki jagah chhodkar sirf kinaare ki bhujayein jodi
did.en: left out the inside and added up only the sides round the edge

why.hi: dhaaga sirf kinaare par chalta hai: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm
why.en: the thread only goes on the edge: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm

whyAlt.hi: Ulta socho: 6 × 4 = 24 toh andar ke chhote square hote, dhaaga nahi; dhaage ke liye 6 do baar aur 4 do baar, yaani 12 aur 8, kul 20 cm.
whyAlt.en: Think the other way: 6 × 4 = 24 would be the little squares inside, not thread; for thread, 6 twice and 4 twice, that is 12 and 8, 20 cm in all.

simpler.hi: Ek kone se dhaaga lapetna shuru karo aur wapas usi kone tak aao; har bhuja par jitna dhaaga khula, woh jodte jao.
simpler.en: Start winding the thread at one corner and come back to the same corner; add up how much thread comes off along each side.

simpler.hi: Socho yeh rectangle ek khet hai: chaaron taraf ki baad parimap hai, aur andar ghaas wali jagah area. Baad naapne mein ghaas ka koi kaam nahi.
simpler.en: Picture this rectangle as a field: the fence all round it is the perimeter, and the grassy space inside is the area. Measuring the fence has nothing to do with the grass.

problem.hi: Phoolon ki ek kyari triangle jaisi hai, bhujayein 7 m, 9 m aur 12 m. Uske kinaare-kinaare ek baar baad lagani hai. Dekhte hain, kitni lambi baad lagegi.
problem.en: A flower bed is a triangle with sides 7 m, 9 m and 12 m. A fence goes once along its edge. We see how long the fence will be.

problemAlt.hi: Socho tum kyari ke ek kone par khade ho. 7 m chalo, mudo, 9 m chalo, mudo, phir 12 m chal ke wahin pahunch jao. Baad utni hi lambi chahiye jitna tum chale, toh wahi doori nikalni hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture standing at one corner of the bed. Walk 7 m, turn, walk 9 m, turn, then walk 12 m back to where you began. The fence is as long as that walk, so that distance is what we find.

simpler.hi: Ek chhoti cheez se socho: rumaal ke chaaron taraf lace lagani ho, toh lace har bhuja par lagti hai, aur kul lace un sab bhujaon ka jod hoti hai. Kyari ki baad bhi aisi hi hai, bas bhujayein teen hain.
simpler.en: Think of something small first: to put lace all round a handkerchief, the lace goes on every side, and all the lace is the sum of those sides. The bed's fence is just like that, only with three sides.

givens.hi: teeno bhujayein pata hain, sab metre mein
givens.en: all three sides are known, all in metres

find.hi: kyari ka parimap, wahi baad ki lambai hai
find.en: the bed's perimeter; that is the length of the fence

do.hi: Baad kinaare par lagegi, toh teeno bhujayein jodni hain
do.en: The fence goes along the edge, so all three sides get added

why.hi: ek bhi bhuja chhooti toh baad mein wahan khaali jagah reh jaayegi
why.en: miss even one side and the fence has a gap there

simpler.hi: Socho baad ki jaali teen roll mein aayi hai: ek 7 m, ek 9 m, ek 12 m. Har bhuja par ek roll khulta hai, toh poori baad teeno roll milakar banti hai.
simpler.en: Picture the fence netting arriving in three rolls: one 7 m, one 9 m, one 12 m. One roll opens out on each side, so the whole fence is all three rolls together.

prompt.hi: Pehle 7 aur 9 jodo: kitne metre hue?
prompt.en: First add 7 and 9: how many metres is that?

right.hi: Haan, 7 + 9 = 16 m; do bhujayein jud gayi.
right.en: Yes, 7 + 9 = 16 m; two sides are added.

why.hi: do bhujayein ho gayi, teesri abhi baaki hai
why.en: two sides done, the third is still to go

simpler.hi: Kyari ke ek kone se chalo: pehle 7 m wali bhuja, phir mud ke 9 m wali, aur ab tak 16 m hue. 12 m wali bhuja par abhi pair nahi rakha.
simpler.en: Walk from a corner of the bed: the 7 m side, then turn onto the 9 m side, and that is 16 m so far. The 12 m side is still ahead.

prompt.hi: Teesri bhuja bachi, 12 m. 16 mein 12 jodo, kitna hua?
prompt.en: The third side is left, 12 m. Add 12 to 16: what do you get?

did.hi: teesri bhuja jodkar kyari ki poori baad nikali
did.en: added the third side to find the bed's whole fence

simpler.hi: 16 m mein abhi sirf do bhujayein hain, 7 m aur 9 m. Teesri bhuja 12 m bhi kinaare par hai, use bhi jodna hai.
simpler.en: 16 m has only two sides so far, 7 m and 9 m. The third side, 12 m, is on the edge too, so add it as well.

why.hi: 7 + 9 + 12 = 28 m, teeno bhujayein judi, poori baad ban gayi
why.en: 7 + 9 + 12 = 28 m: all three sides in, the whole fence done

whyAlt.hi: 16 mein pehle 4 jodo toh 20, phir bache 8 jodo toh 28 m; 12 mein se kuch nahi chhoota.
whyAlt.en: Add 4 to 16 first to make 20, then the remaining 8 to make 28 m; no part of the 12 is left out.

answer.hi: kyari ke liye 28 m lambi baad
answer.en: 28 m of fence for the bed

why.hi: baad ko teeno bhujaon par chalna hai, ek bhi bhuja chhoot nahi sakti
why.en: the fence has to run along all three sides; not one side can be skipped

viewCaption.hi: Kyari ki baad ko seedha kholo toh aisi dikhegi: 7 m, 9 m aur 12 m, ek ke baad ek.
viewCaption.en: Straighten out the bed's fence and it looks like this: 7 m, 9 m and 12 m, one after another.

prompt.hi: Ek park ki chaar bhujayein alag-alag lambai ki hain. Ek kone se ghoomo toh: 9 m, 6 m, 7 m aur 4 m. Usi kone par wapas pahunchne tak kitne metre chaloge?
prompt.en: A park has four sides, all of different lengths. Going round from one corner: 9 m, 6 m, 7 m and 4 m. How many metres do you walk to get back to that same corner?

reask.hi: 9 m, 6 m, 7 m aur 4 m bhujaon wale park mein ek kone se ghoom ke wapas usi kone tak kitne metre hote hain?
reask.en: In a park with sides 9 m, 6 m, 7 m and 4 m, how many metres is it from one corner all the way round back to that corner?

did.hi: chaar alag bhujaon wale park ka poora chakkar jodkar nikala
did.en: added up one full round of a park with four different sides

viewCaption.hi: Park ki chaaron bhujayein yahan ek line mein judi hain, pehle 9 m aur aakhir mein 4 m.
viewCaption.en: The park's four sides are joined into one line here, 9 m first and 4 m last.

why.hi: chaaron bhujayein judti hain: 9 + 6 + 7 + 4 = 26 m
why.en: all four sides go in: 9 + 6 + 7 + 4 = 26 m

whyAlt.hi: Jodiyan banao: 9 + 7 = 16 aur 6 + 4 = 10, phir 16 + 10 = 26 m.
whyAlt.en: Pair them up: 9 + 7 = 16 and 6 + 4 = 10, then 16 + 10 = 26 m.

simpler.hi: Kone se chalo aur har bhuja ki lambai jodte jao; chakkar tabhi poora hai jab chaaron bhujayein jud jaayein.
simpler.en: Start at a corner and keep adding each side's length; the round is complete only when all four sides are added.

prompt.en: {friendF} worked out the perimeter of a card 10 cm long and 4 cm wide as 10 × 4 = 40 cm. What is the correct perimeter in centimetres?

reask.hi: 10 cm lambe, 4 cm chaude card ka sahi parimap kitne centimetre hai?

did.hi: card ki bhujayein guna ki jagah jodkar ek galti pakdi
did.en: caught a mistake by adding the card's sides instead of multiplying

viewCaption.hi: Card ki chaaron bhujayein line par hain: 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm, 4 cm. Is line mein sirf kinaara hai, card ke andar ka kuch nahi.
viewCaption.en: The card's four sides are on the line: 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm, 4 cm. This line holds only the edge, nothing from inside the card.

why.hi: parimap kinaara hai: 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 cm; 10 × 4 andar ki jagah hai
why.en: the perimeter is the edge: 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 cm; 10 × 4 is the inside

whyAlt.hi: 10 cm wali do bhujayein 20 cm, 4 cm wali do bhujayein 8 cm, toh parimap 20 + 8 = 28 cm; 40 toh card ke andar ke chhote square ginta hai.
whyAlt.en: The two 10 cm sides make 20 cm and the two 4 cm sides make 8 cm, so the perimeter is 20 + 8 = 28 cm; 40 counts the little squares inside the card.

simpler.hi: Board par card ki chaaron bhujayein dekho, chahe number sirf do par likha ho. Socho, guna ki jagah inke saath kya karna hai.
simpler.en: Look at all four sides of the card on the board, even if only two carry a number. Think what to do with them in place of multiplying.

six unequal edges in a real context (exhibition board tape) → every edge, once

viewCaption.en: The board shows a five-cornered field, with corners P, Q, R, S and T.

say.hi: Ab ek khet socho, kone P, Q, R, S, T. P par ungli rakho aur har bhuja ka naam lo jaise-jaise uski lambai jodte ho. Ek bhi bhuja chhooti toh jod adhoora. Jod tabhi poora hota hai jab tum wapas P par pahunchte ho.
say.en: Now picture a field, corners P, Q, R, S, T. Put a finger on P and name each side as you add its length. Miss one side and the sum is unfinished. The sum is finished only when you are back at P.

simpler.hi: Har bhuja par ungli rakho aur uska naam lo. Jo bhuja bol di, uski lambai jod do.
simpler.en: Put a finger on each side and say its name. Every side you name, add its length.

sayAlt.hi: Ek chowkidaar raat ko khet ke kinaare ghoomta hai aur har kone par seeti bajata hai. Jab tak woh pehle kone par lautke seeti na bajaye, chakkar poora nahi, aur beech ki har bhuja uski doori mein judti hai.
sayAlt.en: A watchman walks the field's edge at night and blows a whistle at every corner. Until he is back at the first corner and whistles there, the round is not done, and every side on the way adds to his distance.

prompt.hi: Khet PQRST ki paanch bhujayein hain: PQ 8 m, QR 5 m, RS 7 m, ST 6 m, TP 3 m. Khet ka poora kinaara kitne metre ka hai?
prompt.en: Field PQRST has five sides: PQ 8 m, QR 5 m, RS 7 m, ST 6 m, TP 3 m. How many metres is the field's whole edge?

reask.hi: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m aur 3 m bhujaon wale khet PQRST ka poora kinaara kitne metre ka hai?
reask.en: How many metres is the whole edge of field PQRST, with sides 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m and 3 m?

viewCaption.hi: Line par khet ki paanchon bhujayein usi kram mein hain jaise P se chalte hain: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m aur 3 m.
viewCaption.en: The field's five sides are on the line in the order you walk them from P: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m and 3 m.

why.hi: P se wapas P tak paanchon bhujayein: 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 29 m
why.en: P back to P, all five sides: 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 29 m

whyAlt.hi: Aasaan jodiyan pehle: 8 + 5 = 13 aur 7 + 3 = 10, toh 23; phir ST ke 6 jodo, 29 m.
whyAlt.en: Easy pairs first: 8 + 5 = 13 and 7 + 3 = 10, so 23; then add ST's 6, 29 m.

simpler.hi: P se shuru karo aur PQ, QR, RS, ST, TP bolte jao. TP ke baad tum wapas P par ho.
simpler.en: Start at P and say PQ, QR, RS, ST, TP as you go. After TP you are back at P.

remediation.move: thread vs tiles, spoken over the then-card's own board (a 14 cm by 9 cm sticker) and naming none of its numbers: thread laid along the edge, then straightened against a ruler = perimeter (cm); tiles laid inside = area; a perimeter question → thread, so add the side lengths, never multiply them; the then-card asks what is left of a 140 cm ribbon

say.hi: Socho, ek rectangle ke kinaare par dhaaga lapeta, phir khol ke scale par rakha: woh lambai parimap hai, centimetre mein. Andar tiles bichhao toh woh area hai. Parimap mein chaaron bhujayein jodte hain, guna nahi.
say.en: Picture a thread wrapped round a rectangle's edge, then laid straight on a ruler: that length is the perimeter, in centimetres. Tiles inside are the area. For the perimeter we add the four sides, not multiply.

simpler.hi: Dhaaga kinaare par, tiles andar. Humein dhaaga chahiye, toh bas chaaron bhujayein jodo.
simpler.en: Thread on the edge, tiles inside. We want the thread, so just add the four sides.

sayAlt.hi: Is rectangle ko ek chhota aangan socho: deewar kinaare par chalti hai, aur andar farsh hai jo area hai. Deewar ki lambai ke liye bhujayein jodte hain; lambai aur chaudai ka guna sirf farsh batata hai.
sayAlt.en: Think of this rectangle as a small courtyard: the wall runs along the edge, and the floor inside is the area. For the wall's length we add the sides; length times breadth only tells the floor.

prompt.hi: Tumhare paas 140 cm ribbon hai. 14 cm lambe, 9 cm chaude sticker ke kinaare-kinaare ribbon lagao. Kitna bachega?
prompt.en: You have 140 cm of ribbon. Put it all along the edge of a sticker 14 cm long and 9 cm wide. How much is left?

reask.hi: 140 cm ribbon mein se 14 cm lambe, 9 cm chaude sticker ke kinaare-kinaare ek baar lagaane ke baad kitna ribbon bachega?
reask.en: Out of 140 cm of ribbon, how much is left after it goes once all along the edge of a sticker 14 cm long and 9 cm wide?

viewCaption.hi: Sticker ka kinaara line par khula hai: 14 cm, 9 cm, 14 cm, 9 cm. Ribbon isi line ke barabar lagega.
viewCaption.en: The sticker's edge is opened out on the line: 14 cm, 9 cm, 14 cm, 9 cm. The ribbon that goes on is as long as this line.

why.hi: kinaare par 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 cm lagega, toh 140 − 46 = 94 cm bachega
why.en: the edge takes 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 cm, so 140 − 46 = 94 cm is left

whyShort.en: the edge takes 46 cm, so 140 − 46 = 94 cm

whyAlt.hi: 14 do baar 28 aur 9 do baar 18, toh kinaare par 46 cm; 140 mein se pehle 40 hatao toh 100, phir 6 aur hatao toh 94 cm.
whyAlt.en: 14 twice is 28 and 9 twice is 18, so the edge takes 46 cm; take 40 from 140 to get 100, then 6 more to get 94 cm.

simpler.hi: Ribbon andar nahi jaata. Pehle dekho kinaare par kitna lagega, phir use 140 mein se ghatao.
simpler.en: The ribbon does not go inside. First find how much the edge takes, then take that from 140.

bridgeToNext.hi: Seedhi bhujaon wali har shape mein har bhuja jodna chalta hai. Ab ek rectangle socho: iski bhujayein jodiyon mein aati hain, aur isse jodne ka ek jaldi wala tareeka milta hai.
bridgeToNext.en: For any shape with straight sides, adding every side works. Now think of a rectangle: its sides come in pairs, and that gives us a quicker way to add.

simpler.hi: Seedhi bhujaon wali shape mein saari bhujayein jodna chalta hai. Rectangle mein bhujayein jodiyon mein aati hain, isse kaam chhota ho jaata hai.
simpler.en: For a shape with straight sides, adding all the sides works. In a rectangle the sides come in pairs, and that makes the work shorter.

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki parimap band shape ke poore kinaare ki lambai hai: har bhuja ek baar, andar ki jagah nahi.
covered.en: Today we saw that perimeter is a closed shape's whole edge: every side once, never the space inside.

hook.convey: rectangle and square boundaries everywhere → their sides repeat → a quicker way than writing all four numbers each time

use.hi: Cricket pitch phir se: 20 m lambi, 3 m chaudi. Kinaare par chalo toh 20 m do baar milta hai, 3 m bhi do baar. Yahi jodi jodne ka jaldi wala tareeka banegi.
use.en: The cricket pitch again: 20 m long, 3 m wide. Walk its edge and you meet 20 m twice, and 3 m twice. That pairing becomes the quicker way to add.

use.hi: Ludo board square hota hai, chaaron bhujayein ek barabar. Ek bhuja pata chal gayi, toh poore board ka parimap bhi pata.
use.en: A ludo board is a square, all four sides the same. Know one side, and you know the perimeter of the whole board.

explain.convey: rectangle (aayat) → opposite sides equal → going round: lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai; 10 m by 6 m → the board labels each length once, but the walk passes each twice

viewCaption.hi: Ek chakkar ki chaaron bhujayein ek line par hain: lambai, chaudai, phir wahi lambai aur chaudai dobara.
viewCaption.en: The four sides of one round are on one line: the length, the breadth, then the same length and breadth again.

prompt.hi: Is rectangle mein 10 m ki kitni bhujayein hain?
prompt.en: How many 10 m sides does this rectangle have?

point.hi: Is rectangle ki do lambi bhujayein 10 m ki hain, woh lambai hai. Do chhoti bhujayein 6 m ki, woh chaudai. Aamne-saamne ki bhujayein barabar hoti hain. 10 aur 6 ek-ek baar likhe hain, par chakkar lagao toh dono do-do baar milte hain.
point.en: This rectangle's two long sides are 10 m each: that is the length. The two short sides are 6 m: that is the breadth. Opposite sides are equal. 10 and 6 are written once, but go round and you meet each twice.

pointAlt.hi: Ek darwaaza socho: uski do lambi bhujayein ek jitni hain, aur do chhoti bhi ek jitni. Yahan bhi wahi baat hai: 10 m wali bhujayein do hain aur 6 m wali bhi do. Ek poora chakkar inhi chaar bhujaon se banta hai.
pointAlt.en: Think of a door: its two long sides match, and its two short sides match too. It is the same here: there are two 10 m sides and two 6 m sides. One full round is made of just these four sides.

prompt.hi: Ek poora chakkar kitne metre ka hua?
prompt.en: How many metres is one full round?

reask.hi: 10 m lambe, 6 m chaude is rectangle ka ek poora chakkar kitne metre ka hai?
reask.en: How many metres is one full round of this rectangle, 10 m long and 6 m wide?

did.hi: rectangle ki lambai aur chaudai do-do baar ginkar chakkar nikala
did.en: counted a rectangle's length and breadth twice each to find one round

why.hi: 10 aur 6 dono do-do baar aate hain: 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m
why.en: 10 and 6 both come twice: 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m

whyAlt.hi: Pehle dono lambai: 10 + 10 = 20, phir dono chaudai: 6 + 6 = 12, aur 20 + 12 = 32 m.
whyAlt.en: Both lengths first: 10 + 10 = 20, then both breadths: 6 + 6 = 12, and 20 + 12 = 32 m.

simpler.hi: Ungli ek kone se ghumao: har mod par ek bhuja khatam hoti hai, aur chaar mod ke baad tum wahin pahunchte ho.
simpler.en: Run your finger round from one corner: each turn ends a side, and after four turns you are back where you began.

simpler.hi: Board par sirf do number likhe hain, par bhujayein chaar hain. Har likhi bhuja ke saamne uski jodidaar bhuja hai, bilkul utni hi lambi.
simpler.en: Only two numbers are written on the board, but there are four sides. Opposite each labelled side is its partner, exactly as long.

explain.convey: one length + one breadth = corner to the opposite corner = HALF the way round; the full round = that half twice → P = 2 × (l + b); on a new 12 m by 5 m rectangle the child does 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 m; l + b alone = 17 m = only half the boundary

viewCaption.hi: Is line ki pehli do bhujayein, 12 m aur 5 m, aadha chakkar hain. Baaki do bhujayein bilkul unhi jaisi hain.
viewCaption.en: The first two sides on this line, 12 m and 5 m, are half a round. The other two sides are exactly the same.

prompt.hi: Aadhe chakkar mein lambai kitni baar aati hai?
prompt.en: In half a round, how many times does the length come?

say.hi: Aadhe chakkar mein lambai ek baar aati hai.
say.en: In half a round the length comes once.

point.hi: Naya rectangle: 12 m lamba, 5 m chauda. Neeche baayein kone se chalo, 12 m aage, phir 5 m upar. Ab tum saamne wale kone par ho, yaani aadha chakkar. Baaki aadha bhi utna hi lamba hai. Isliye parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai).
point.en: New rectangle: 12 m long, 5 m wide. From the bottom-left corner go 12 m along, then 5 m up. Now you are at the opposite corner: half a round. The other half is as long. So perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

pointAlt.hi: Is rectangle ki chaar bhujaon ko do jodiyon mein baanto: ek 12 m aur ek 5 m ki jodi, aur waisi hi doosri jodi. Ek jodi ka jod lo aur uska do guna karo: yahi 2 × (lambai + chaudai) hai.
pointAlt.en: Split this rectangle's four sides into two pairs: one 12 m and one 5 m in a pair, and a second pair the same. Take one pair's sum and double it: that is 2 × (length + breadth).

prompt.hi: 2 × (lambai + chaudai) lagao: is rectangle ke liye yeh kitna banta hai?
prompt.en: Use 2 × (length + breadth): what does it come to for this rectangle?

did.hi: 2 × (lambai + chaudai) se rectangle ka parimap nikala
did.en: used 2 × (length + breadth) to find a rectangle's perimeter

why.hi: aadha chakkar 12 + 5 = 17 m, aur uska do guna: 2 × 17 = 34 m
why.en: half a round is 12 + 5 = 17 m, and double that: 2 × 17 = 34 m

whyShort.hi: aadha chakkar 17 m, do guna 34 m
whyShort.en: half a round is 17 m, double is 34 m

whyAlt.hi: Chaaron bhujayein jodke jaancho: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 m, wahi jo formula deta hai.
whyAlt.en: Check by adding all four sides: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 m, the same as the formula gives.

simpler.hi: Formula mein bracket pehle: usmein lambai aur chaudai jaati hain. Phir bracket ka do guna.
simpler.en: In the formula the bracket comes first: the length and breadth go in it. Then twice the bracket.

simpler.hi: Ek kone se saamne wale kone tak do raaste hain, ek neeche se aur ek upar se. Dono mein ek lambai aur ek chaudai hai, isliye dono barabar, aur dono milke poora chakkar.
simpler.en: From a corner to the opposite one there are two ways: along the bottom or the top. Each takes one length and one breadth, so they are equal and together make the full round.

explain.convey: square (varg) → all 4 sides equal → side + side + side + side = 4 × side; the answer is a length → cm, not square cm; square of side 6 cm

viewCaption.hi: Is line mein square ki chaaron bhujayein ek jaisi lambi dikhti hain, har ek 6 cm.
viewCaption.en: On this line the square's four sides all look the same length, each 6 cm.

prompt.hi: Is square ke kinaare mein 6 cm ki bhuja kitni baar aati hai?
prompt.en: How many times does the 6 cm side come in this square's edge?

say.hi: 6 cm ki bhuja chaar baar aati hai.
say.en: The 6 cm side comes four times.

point.hi: Square ki chaaron bhujayein barabar hoti hain, yahan har ek 6 cm. 6 ko chaar baar jodne se achha, seedha 4 × bhuja. Aur jawab ek lambai hai, toh centimetre mein aayega, square centimetre mein nahi.
point.en: A square's four sides are all equal; here each is 6 cm. Rather than adding 6 four times, just do 4 × side. And the answer is a length, so it comes in cm, not square cm.

pointAlt.hi: Square ko aisa rectangle maano jiski lambai bhi 6 cm hai aur chaudai bhi. Toh pichhla formula yahan bhi chalega: 2 × (6 + 6), wahi chaar bhujayein. Yeh kinaare ki lambai hai, isliye jawab centimetre mein, square centimetre mein nahi.
pointAlt.en: Take the square as a rectangle with length 6 cm and breadth 6 cm too. The last formula works here as well: 2 × (6 + 6), the same four sides. This is the edge's length, so the answer is in centimetres, not square centimetres.

prompt.hi: Ek bhuja 6 cm hai, toh chaaron bhujaon ki kul lambai kitni hai?
prompt.en: One side is 6 cm, so what is the total length of all four sides?

did.hi: square ki chaaron bhujaon ki kul lambai nikali
did.en: found the total length of a square's four sides

why.hi: chaar bhujayein, har ek 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm, lambai hai isliye cm
why.en: four sides of 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm, a length, so cm

whyShort.hi: chaar bhujayein, har ek 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm

whyAlt.hi: Har bhuja par 6 aur jodte jao: 6, 12, 18, 24, toh 24 cm; yeh kinaare ki lambai hai, isliye centimetre, square centimetre nahi.
whyAlt.en: Add 6 for each side: 6, 12, 18, 24, so 24 cm; it is the length of the edge, so centimetres, not square centimetres.

simpler.hi: 6 cm ki chaar bhujaon ko ek seedhi line mein khol kar socho. Woh line kitni lambi hogi, wahi jawab hai.
simpler.en: Picture the four 6 cm sides opened out into one straight line. How long that line is, is the answer.

simpler.hi: Square mein ek bhuja jaan lo toh baaki teen bhi pata, kyunki sab barabar hain. Aur dhaage ko scale par naapte hain, isliye jawab centimetre mein aata hai, square centimetre mein nahi.
simpler.en: In a square, know one side and you know the other three, because they are all equal. And a thread is measured on a ruler, so the answer comes in centimetres, not square centimetres.

problem.hi: Ek notebook ka cover rectangle hai, 24 cm lamba aur 18 cm chauda. Uske kinaare par ek baar tape lagani hai. Dekhte hain kitni tape lagegi.
problem.en: A notebook cover is a rectangle, 24 cm long and 18 cm wide. Tape goes once along its edge. We find how much tape it takes.

problemAlt.hi: Socho cover ke ek kone se tape chipkaana shuru kiya: 24 cm lambai, 18 cm chaudai, phir 24 aur 18 wapas. Shuru wale kone tak aate-aate roll se jitni tape khulegi, wahi nikalni hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture starting the tape at one corner of the cover: 24 cm along, 18 cm down, then 24 and 18 back. However much tape comes off the roll by the time it reaches that corner again is what we find.

simpler.hi: Pehle ek chhota rectangle socho, 2 cm lamba aur 1 cm chauda. Uske kinaare par tape 2, 1, 2 aur 1 cm, yaani 6 cm lagegi. Cover bhi aisa hi hai, bas uski bhujayein badi hain.
simpler.en: First picture a small rectangle, 2 cm long and 1 cm wide. Tape round its edge is 2, 1, 2 and 1 cm, that is 6 cm. The cover is just the same, only its sides are bigger.

givens.hi: lambai aur chaudai pata hai, dono centimetre mein
givens.en: the length and the breadth are known, both in cm

find.hi: cover ka parimap, utni hi tape lagegi
find.en: the cover's perimeter; that is how much tape

do.hi: Cover rectangle hai, toh 2 × (lambai + chaudai) lagao
do.en: The cover is a rectangle, so use 2 × (length + breadth)

why.hi: chakkar mein lambai do baar milti hai, chaudai bhi do baar
why.en: going round, you meet the length twice and the breadth twice

simpler.hi: Tape ek kone se chalao: 24 aur 18 cm ke baad tum saamne wale kone par ho. Wapas aane mein phir 24 aur 18, yaani wahi jod do baar.
simpler.en: Run the tape from a corner: after 24 and 18 cm you are at the opposite corner. Coming back is 24 and 18 again, the same sum twice.

prompt.hi: Bracket pehle: 24 + 18 kitna hua?
prompt.en: The bracket first: what is 24 + 18?

right.hi: Haan, 42 cm: ek lambai aur ek chaudai.
right.en: Yes, 42 cm: one length and one breadth.

why.hi: ek lambai aur ek chaudai jodne se aadha chakkar milta hai, aur poora chakkar usi aadhe ka do guna hai
why.en: one length plus one breadth gives half a round, and the full round is twice that half

simpler.hi: 24 aur 18 ko upar-neeche likho, aur ikaai se shuru karke jodo.
simpler.en: Write 24 and 18 one under the other and add, starting with the ones.

prompt.hi: Yeh toh aadha chakkar tha. Poore chakkar ke liye 2 × 42 kitna hoga?
prompt.en: That was only half a round. For the full round, what is 2 × 42?

did.hi: aadhe chakkar ka do guna karke poori tape nikali
did.en: doubled half a round to find the whole tape

simpler.hi: 42 ko do baar jodo: 42 + 42.
simpler.en: Add 42 twice: 42 + 42.

why.hi: aadha chakkar 42 cm, poora chakkar 2 × 42 = 84 cm
why.en: half a round is 42 cm, the full round 2 × 42 = 84 cm

whyAlt.hi: 42 + 42 mein pehle 40 + 40 = 80, phir 2 + 2 = 4, toh poore kinaare ke liye 84 cm.
whyAlt.en: In 42 + 42, first 40 + 40 = 80, then 2 + 2 = 4, so 84 cm for the whole edge.

answer.en: 84 cm of tape for the cover

why.en: round a rectangle, the length and the breadth each come twice

prompt.hi: {friendF} ne 40 m lambe, 25 m chaude playground ka ek chakkar daud ke kaha ki 65 m hua. Sahi mein woh kitne metre daudi?
prompt.en: {friendF} ran once round a playground 40 m long and 25 m wide and said it was 65 m. How many metres did she really run?

did.hi: 65 m ko aadha chakkar pehchaana aur poora chakkar nikala
did.en: saw 65 m was only half a round, and found the whole

why.hi: aadha chakkar 40 + 25 = 65 m, poora chakkar 2 × 65 = 130 m

whyShort.en: half a round 65 m, full round 130 m

whyAlt.en: Run one side at a time: 40 + 25 = 65, then 65 + 40 = 105, and 105 + 25 = 130 m.

simpler.hi: Socho, ek lambai aur ek chaudai daud kar woh kis kone par pahunchti hai, aur wahan se shuru wala kona kitna door hai.
simpler.en: Think which corner she reaches after running one length and one breadth, and how far the starting corner still is from there.

prompt.hi: Laal card 16 cm lamba, 9 cm chauda hai, aur neela card 20 cm lamba, 6 cm chauda. Dono ke poore kinaare par golden border lagani hai. Kiski border lambi hogi, laal ki ya neele ki?
prompt.en: The red card is 16 cm long and 9 cm wide, and the blue card is 20 cm long and 6 cm wide. A golden border goes along the whole edge of each. Whose border is longer, the red one's or the blue one's?

reask.hi: Laal card 16 cm lamba, 9 cm chauda, aur neela 20 cm lamba, 6 cm chauda: kiski border lambi hogi, laal ki ya neele ki?
reask.en: The red card is 16 cm by 9 cm and the blue one 20 cm by 6 cm: whose border is longer, the red one's or the blue one's?

did.hi: do cardon ke parimap compare karke lambi border wala card chuna
did.en: compared two cards' perimeters and picked the one with the longer border

viewCaption.hi: Baayein taraf laal card ki lambai aur chaudai likhi hai, daayein taraf neele card ki. Border har card ke poore kinaare par lagegi, andar nahi.
viewCaption.en: The red card's length and breadth are written on the left, the blue card's on the right. Each border goes along the card's whole edge, not inside.

why.hi: laal 2 × (16 + 9) = 50 cm, neela 2 × (20 + 6) = 52 cm; neele ki border lambi
why.en: red 2 × (16 + 9) = 50 cm, blue 2 × (20 + 6) = 52 cm: blue's is longer

whyShort.hi: laal 50 cm, neela 52 cm; neele ki border lambi

whyAlt.hi: Sirf aadha chakkar milaao: laal ka 16 + 9 = 25 aur neele ka 20 + 6 = 26; aadha chakkar neele ka bada hai, toh poora bhi neele ka bada.

simpler.hi: Andar ki jagah mat dekho, sirf kinaara. Har card ki lambai aur chaudai jodo, phir dono jod milaao.

why.hi: chaar barabar bhujayein: 4 × 11 = 44 cm, aur jawab centimetre mein

remediation.move: ant walk with a running counter instead of a formula, spoken over the then-card's own board (a 19 m by 8 m field) and naming none of its numbers: the ant starts at a corner, walks the length, then the breadth, and is only at the opposite corner, halfway (l + b stops here); home is still two sides away; then the then-card's field all round

say.hi: Socho, ek cheenti khet ke kone se chalti hai aur metre ginti jaati hai. Pehle lambai chali, phir chaudai: ab woh saamne wale kone par hai, bas aadha chakkar. Lambai + chaudai yahin tak hai. Shuru wala kona abhi do bhujayein door hai.
say.en: Picture an ant starting at a field's corner and counting the metres. First the length, then the breadth: now it is at the opposite corner, half a round. Length + breadth stops here. Its starting corner is two sides away.

simpler.hi: Saamne wala kona shuru wala kona nahi hai. Cheenti ko abhi do bhujayein aur chalni hain.
simpler.en: The opposite corner is not where it started. The ant still has two more sides to walk.

sayAlt.hi: Ek dhaage se rectangle ka poora kinaara banao, phir dhaage ko beech se mod ke do barabar tukde karo. Ek tukde mein bas ek lambai aur ek chaudai aati hai; lambai + chaudai mude hue dhaage jitna hai, poore dhaage jitna nahi.
sayAlt.en: Make the whole edge of a rectangle from a thread, then fold the thread in the middle into two equal parts. One part holds just one length and one breadth; length + breadth is as long as the folded thread, not the whole thread.

prompt.hi: Cheenti 19 m lambe aur 8 m chaude khet ka ek poora chakkar lagati hai. Woh kul kitne metre chali?
prompt.en: An ant goes once all round a field 19 m long and 8 m wide. How many metres did it walk in all?

reask.hi: 19 m lambe, 8 m chaude khet ka chakkar poora karke cheenti shuru wale kone par lauti; woh kul kitne metre chali?
reask.en: An ant goes all round a field 19 m long and 8 m wide and is back at its starting corner; how many metres did it walk in all?

viewCaption.hi: Cheenti jin chaar bhujaon par chalti hai, woh yahan ek line mein hain: 19 m, 8 m, 19 m, 8 m.
viewCaption.en: The four sides the ant walks are here in one line: 19 m, 8 m, 19 m, 8 m.

why.hi: do lambai aur do chaudai: 19 + 8 + 19 + 8 = 54 m
why.en: two lengths and two breadths: 19 + 8 + 19 + 8 = 54 m

whyShort.hi: do lambai aur do chaudai jodkar 54 m
whyShort.en: two lengths and two breadths make 54 m

whyAlt.hi: Cheenti 19 + 8 = 27 m par saamne wale kone par thi, aur shuru wale kone tak phir 27 m: 27 + 27 = 54 m.
whyAlt.en: The ant was at the opposite corner at 19 + 8 = 27 m, and back to its starting corner is another 27 m: 27 + 27 = 54 m.

simpler.hi: Board par dekho, cheenti ka poora chakkar kin bhujaon se banta hai; phir unki lambai jodo.
simpler.en: See on the board which sides make the ant's whole round; then add their lengths.

remediation.move: the unit test, spoken over the then-card's own board (an 11 cm by 2 cm bookmark) and naming none of its numbers: a thread is measured on a ruler → centimetres (the edge); little 1 cm squares are counted → square centimetres (area); an edge question → add the sides; then the then-card's bookmark

say.hi: Parimap aur area ko jawab ki ikaai se pehchaano. Socho, dhaage ko scale par naapa, toh kinaara centimetre mein aaya; andar ke 1 cm wale square gine, toh area square centimetre mein. Kinaare ka sawaal ho toh bhujayein jodo.
say.en: Tell perimeter and area apart by the answer's unit. A thread is measured on a ruler, so the edge comes in centimetres; the 1 cm squares inside are counted, so area comes in square centimetres. For the edge, add the sides.

simpler.hi: Kinaara rassi jaisa hai aur andar ki jagah chatai jaisi. Rassi centimetre mein naapte hain, chatai square centimetre mein.
simpler.en: The edge is like a rope and the space inside like a mat. A rope is measured in centimetres, a mat in square centimetres.

sayAlt.hi: Ek chocolate ke wrapper ko socho: uske kinaare ki sunehri line scale se centimetre mein naapte hain, aur andar ki chocolate ke chhote square gine jaate hain. Line ke liye bhujayein judti hain; guna sirf andar ke square ginta hai.
sayAlt.en: Think of a chocolate wrapper: the golden line round its edge is measured with a ruler in centimetres, and the little squares of chocolate inside are counted. For the line the sides are added; multiplying only counts the squares inside.

prompt.hi: Ek bookmark 11 cm lamba, 2 cm chauda hai. Uske kinaare ki poori lambai kitne centimetre hai?
prompt.en: A bookmark is 11 cm long and 2 cm wide. How many centimetres long is its whole edge?

reask.hi: 11 cm lambe, 2 cm chaude bookmark ke kinaare ki poori lambai kitne centimetre hai?
reask.en: How many centimetres long is the whole edge of a bookmark 11 cm long and 2 cm wide?

viewCaption.hi: Bookmark ke kinaare ko scale ki tarah seedha kiya hai: 11 cm, 2 cm, 11 cm, 2 cm.
viewCaption.en: The bookmark's edge is laid straight like a ruler: 11 cm, 2 cm, 11 cm, 2 cm.

why.hi: kinaara centimetre mein naapte hain aur bhujayein judti hain: 11 + 2 + 11 + 2 = 26 cm
why.en: the edge is measured in centimetres and the sides are added: 11 + 2 + 11 + 2 = 26 cm

whyAlt.hi: 11 aur 2 se aadha chakkar 13 cm, aur poora uska do guna, 26 cm; 11 × 2 = 22 toh andar ke square centimetre hain.
whyAlt.en: 11 and 2 make half a round, 13 cm, and the whole is double that, 26 cm; 11 × 2 = 22 is the square centimetres inside.

simpler.hi: 11 × 2 andar ke square centimetre deta hai. Kinaare ke liye bookmark ki chaaron bhujayein socho.
simpler.en: 11 × 2 gives the square centimetres inside. For the edge, think of all four sides of the bookmark.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab parimap ko kaam mein lagayenge: kabhi usse ulta ek bhuja nikalni hogi, kabhi chakkaron ki doori ya taar ka hisaab.
bridgeToNext.en: Now we put the perimeter to work: sometimes we work back from it to a side, sometimes we find the distance of rounds or the wire.

simpler.hi: Agle sawaalon mein parimap se aage kaam hai: ek bhuja, chakkar, ya taar.
simpler.en: The next questions take the perimeter further: a side, rounds, or wire.

covered.hi: Phir rectangle ka parimap 2 × (lambai + chaudai) aaya, aur square ka 4 × bhuja.
covered.en: Then came a rectangle's perimeter, 2 × (length + breadth), and a square's, 4 × side.

hook.convey: real boundary jobs → perimeter is the first number, then one more step: rounds × perimeter, metres × rate, or perimeter back to a side

use.hi: Football ground rectangle hota hai. Uske teen chakkar daudne ki doori nikalni ho, toh pehle ek chakkar, yaani parimap, phir usko teen se guna.
use.en: A football ground is a rectangle. To find the distance for three rounds of it, first one round, the perimeter, then times three.

use.hi: Garden ki kyari par taar lagani ho toh taar metre ke hisaab se milti hai. Pehle parimap nikalo, phir har metre ka daam lagao.
use.en: To put wire round a garden bed, you buy the wire by the metre. Find the perimeter first, then put the price on each metre.

use.hi: Cricket pitch ke kinaare rassi lagani hai. Pitch 20 m lambi, 3 m chaudi, toh 2 × (20 + 3) = 46 m rassi. Daam ki baat uske baad.
use.en: A rope goes round the edge of a cricket pitch. The pitch is 20 m long and 3 m wide, so 2 × (20 + 3) = 46 m of rope. The price comes after that.

explain.convey: backward for a square: perimeter 60 m shared by 4 equal sides → one side = perimeter ÷ 4 (not ÷ 2); the child does 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m on the board's square

viewCaption.hi: Board par ek square hai, aur uske poore kinaare par 60 m likha hai. Uski chaaron bhujayein barabar hain.
viewCaption.en: The board shows a square with 60 m written for its whole edge. Its four sides are equal.

prompt.hi: 60 m ka poora kinaara kitni barabar bhujaon se bana hai?
prompt.en: How many equal sides make up the whole 60 m edge?

say.hi: Poora kinaara chaar barabar bhujaon se bana hai.
say.en: The whole edge is made of four equal sides.

point.hi: Is square ka parimap, yaani poora kinaara, 60 m hai. Yeh poora kinaara chaar barabar bhujaon se bana hai, do se nahi. Chaaron bhujayein barabar hain, toh 60 m chaaron mein barabar bat-ta hai.
point.en: This square's perimeter, its whole edge, is 60 m. That whole edge is made of four equal sides, not two. All four sides are equal, so the 60 m is shared equally among the four.

pointAlt.hi: Socho 60 m ki ek rassi se yeh square banaya hai. Rassi chaar barabar bhujaon mein mudti hai, toh har bhuja ko rassi ka ek-chauthai milta hai.
pointAlt.en: Imagine this square made from a 60 m rope. The rope bends into four equal sides, so each side gets a quarter of the rope.

prompt.hi: Is square ki ek bhuja kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: How long is one side of this square?

reask.hi: Jis square ka parimap 60 m hai, uski ek bhuja kitni lambi hai?
reask.en: A square has a perimeter of 60 m; how long is one side?

did.hi: square ke parimap ko chaar barabar bhujaon mein baanta
did.en: shared a square's perimeter among its four equal sides

why.hi: 60 m chaar barabar bhujaon mein: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m
why.en: 60 m in four equal parts: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m

whyAlt.hi: Ulta jaancho: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m, toh har bhuja 15 m hi hai.
whyAlt.en: Check it backwards: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m, so each side is indeed 15 m.

simpler.hi: Ulta socho: kaunsa number chaar baar jodne par 60 banta hai.
simpler.en: Think backwards: which number, added four times, makes 60.

simpler.hi: Square ka poora kinaara chaar barabar bhujaon se banta hai, toh ek bhuja poore kinaare ka ek-chauthai hai. Do mein baantoge toh har aadhe mein do bhujayein aa jaayengi.
simpler.en: A square's whole edge is made of four equal sides, so one side is a quarter of the whole edge. Split it in two and each part holds two sides.

explain.convey: backward for a rectangle: perimeter 60 m, length 20 m → half a round = one length + one breadth → the child halves 60 and takes away the length (30 − 20 = 10 m) on the board's rectangle; the point names the two steps and does neither

viewCaption.hi: Is rectangle ki ek bhuja par 20 m likha hai, yahi lambai hai. Poore kinaare ka naap 60 m likha hai.
viewCaption.en: One side of this rectangle says 20 m: that is the length. The whole edge is marked 60 m.

prompt.hi: Aadhe chakkar mein lambai ke saath aur kya aata hai?
prompt.en: In half a round, what comes along with the length?

say.hi: Aadhe chakkar mein ek lambai aur ek chaudai aati hai.
say.en: Half a round holds one length and one breadth.

point.hi: Ab ek rectangle: parimap 60 m, lambai 20 m. Poore chakkar mein do lambai aur do chaudai aati hain, toh aadhe chakkar mein ek lambai aur ek chaudai.
point.en: Now a rectangle: perimeter 60 m, length 20 m. A full round holds two lengths and two breadths, so half a round holds one length and one breadth.

pointAlt.hi: Socho 60 m ki ek rassi se yeh rectangle banaya hai. Aadha chakkar poora hote-hote rassi ek lambai aur ek chaudai ban chuki hoti hai. Lambai 20 m pata hai, toh aadhe chakkar mein se jo bachta hai, wahi chaudai hai.
pointAlt.en: Imagine this rectangle made from a 60 m rope. By half a round the rope has made one length and one breadth. The length is 20 m, so what is left of that half round is the breadth.

prompt.hi: Is rectangle ki chaudai kitni hai?
prompt.en: What is this rectangle's breadth?

reask.hi: 60 m parimap aur 20 m lambai wale rectangle ki chaudai kitni hai?
reask.en: What is the breadth of a rectangle with a 60 m perimeter and a 20 m length?

did.hi: aadhe chakkar se lambai hatakar chaudai nikali
did.en: took the length out of half a round to find the breadth

why.hi: aadha chakkar 30 m, usme se lambai 20 m gayi, bache 10 m
why.en: half a round is 30 m; take away the 20 m length and 10 m is left

whyShort.hi: aadha chakkar 30 m, usme se 20 gaye: 10 m
whyShort.en: half a round is 30, minus 20: 10 m

whyAlt.hi: Jodke dekho: 20 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 60 m, poora parimap mil gaya, toh chaudai 10 m hai.
whyAlt.en: Add it up: 20 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 60 m, the whole perimeter, so the breadth is 10 m.

simpler.hi: Chhote numbers se socho: chakkar 16 m aur lambai 5 m ho, toh aadha 8, aur 8 mein se 5 gaye, 3 bache. Yahan bhi wahi karo.
simpler.en: Try small numbers: if the round were 16 m and the length 5 m, half is 8, and 5 from 8 leaves 3. Do the same here.

simpler.hi: Poore chakkar mein lambai do baar aur chaudai do baar aati hai, toh aadhe chakkar mein dono ek-ek baar. Us aadhe mein se lambai alag kar do, jo bacha woh sirf chaudai hai.
simpler.en: A full round takes in the length twice and the breadth twice, so half a round takes each once. Take the length out of that half, and what is left is only the breadth.

explain.convey: fencing cost = perimeter (m) × rate (₹ per m); 12 m by 8 m plot → 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m of edge at ₹10 per m; a 2 m gate with no wire → subtract it before multiplying: the child works out (40 − 2) × 10 = ₹380

params.mixup: is bhuja mein 2 m ka gate

viewCaption.hi: Plot ka poora kinaara ek line par khula hai: 12 m, 8 m, 12 m, 8 m, kul 40 m. Yeh poora kinaara hai, gate wali jagah bhi isi 40 m mein gini hai.
viewCaption.en: The plot's whole edge is opened out on one line: 12 m, 8 m, 12 m, 8 m, 40 m in all. This is the whole edge; the gate's stretch is counted in these 40 m too.

prompt.hi: Gate kitne metre ka hai?
prompt.en: How many metres is the gate?

point.hi: Plot 12 m lamba, 8 m chauda hai, toh kinaara 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. Taar ₹10 per metre hai, aur kharcha sirf lagne wali taar ka. Par neeche wali bhuja mein 2 m ka gate hai, jahan taar nahi lagti.
point.en: The plot is 12 m by 8 m, so the edge is 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. Wire is ₹10 per metre, paid only for wire that goes on. But the bottom side has a 2 m gate, where no wire goes.

pointAlt.hi: Gate ek darwaaza hai jo khulta hai; wahan taar lagi toh woh khulega hi nahi. Isliye pehle poora kinaara nikalo, 2 × (12 + 8) se, phir gate ke 2 m chhod do. Bachi taar ke hi ₹10 per metre dene hain.
pointAlt.en: The gate is a door that opens; put wire there and it can never open. So first work out the whole edge with 2 × (12 + 8), then leave out the gate's 2 m. We pay ₹10 a metre only for the wire left.

prompt.hi: Gate chhod ke, taar par kul kharcha kitne rupaye aayega?
prompt.en: Leaving out the gate, how many rupees will the wire cost in all?

reask.hi: 12 m lambe, 8 m chaude plot mein 2 m ka gate hai aur taar ₹10 per metre hai; gate chhod ke taar ka kharcha kitna hoga?
reask.en: A plot 12 m long and 8 m wide has a 2 m gate, and wire is ₹10 per metre; leaving out the gate, what does the wire cost?

did.hi: gate chhod kar baaki kinaare ka kharcha nikala
did.en: worked out the cost of the edge left after the gate

why.hi: taar 40 − 2 = 38 m lagegi, aur ₹10 per metre se kharcha 38 × 10 = ₹380
why.en: the wire is 40 − 2 = 38 m, so at ₹10 a metre the cost is 38 × 10 = ₹380

whyAlt.hi: Ulta socho: gate na hota toh poore 40 m ka kharcha ₹400 hota; gate ke 2 m ke ₹20 bach gaye, toh ₹400 − ₹20 = ₹380.
whyAlt.en: Think of it the other way: with no gate the whole 40 m would cost ₹400; the gate's 2 m saves ₹20, so ₹400 − ₹20 = ₹380.

simpler.hi: Ulta bhi soch sakte ho: poore 40 m ka kharcha nikalo, phir gate ke 2 m ka kharcha usmein se ghatao.
simpler.en: You can also think backwards: find the cost of the whole 40 m, then take away the cost of the gate's 2 m.

simpler.hi: Socho plot ke chaaron taraf taar lag rahi hai, aur gate wali 2 m jagah par lakdi ka gate pehle se laga hai. Taar sirf baaki kinaare par chahiye, toh kharcha bhi sirf usi ka.
simpler.en: Picture wire going up all round the plot, with a wooden gate already in its 2 m gap. Wire is needed only on the rest of the edge, so the cost is only for that.

problem.hi: Rani ek rectangle park ke teen chakkar daudti hai. Park 50 m lamba aur 30 m chauda hai. Saath mein uski doori nikaalte hain.
problem.en: Rani runs three rounds of a rectangular park. The park is 50 m long and 30 m wide. Let us work out her distance together.

problemAlt.hi: Rani ka ek chakkar matlab park ke kinaare par ek baar ghoomna: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m. Woh aisa teen baar karti hai. Teeno chakkar milake woh jitna daudti hai, wahi nikalna hai.
problemAlt.en: One round for Rani is going once along the park's edge: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m. She does that three times. What she runs in the three rounds together is what we find.

simpler.hi: Chhote number se socho: agar park ka ek chakkar 10 m hota, toh teen chakkar 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 m hote. Yahan bhi wahi do kaam hain: pehle ek chakkar ki lambai, phir use teen baar.
simpler.en: Try a small number: if one round of the park were 10 m, three rounds would be 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 m. It is the same two jobs here: first the length of one round, then that three times.

givens.hi: park ka naap pata hai, aur chakkar teen hain
givens.en: the park's size is known, and there are three rounds

find.en: the total distance for three rounds

why.hi: Rani kinaare par daudti hai, park ke beech se nahi

simpler.en: Rani plants a flag at one corner and runs, and the round is done only when she has run all four sides back to the flag. So in one round each side comes once.

prompt.hi: Aadha chakkar matlab ek lambai aur ek chaudai. 50 + 30 kitna?

right.hi: Haan, 80 m: yeh aadha chakkar hua.

do.hi: Pehle aadha chakkar: ek lambai aur ek chaudai jodo
do.en: First half a round: add one length and one breadth

why.hi: ek lambai aur ek chaudai milkar aadha chakkar hain
why.en: one length and one breadth together make half a round

simpler.hi: Paison se socho: ₹50 aur ₹30 milke ₹80 hote hain. Waise hi 50 m aur 30 m milke 80 m.
simpler.en: Think of money: ₹50 and ₹30 make ₹80. In the same way, 50 m and 30 m make 80 m.

do.hi: Phir poora chakkar: aadhe chakkar ko do baar lo

why.hi: do aadhe chakkar milke ek poora chakkar

simpler.hi: Do guna matlab wahi number do baar jodna: 80 + 80 = 160. Yeh wahi hai jo 2 × 80 deta hai.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: Rani ne aise teen chakkar daude. Woh kul kitne metre daudi?
prompt.en: Your turn: Rani ran three such rounds. How many metres did she run in all?

simpler.en: All three rounds are the same. Think what to do with one round's distance for three rounds.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh line Rani ka sirf ek chakkar hai: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m, kul 160 m.

answer.en: 480 m in all for the three rounds

why.hi: ek chakkar park ka parimap hai, 160 m, aur teen chakkar uske teen guna

viewCaption.hi: Rani ka ek chakkar yahan ek seedhi line ban gaya hai: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m.

prompt.hi: Ek square garden ke chaaron taraf kul 84 m baad lagi. Har bhuja par kitne metre baad lagi?
prompt.en: 84 m of fence went all round a square garden. How many metres of fence went on each side?

reask.hi: 84 m baad ek square garden ki chaaron barabar bhujaon par lagi; ek bhuja par kitne metre baad hai?

did.hi: 84 m baad ko square ki chaar barabar bhujaon mein baanta
did.en: shared 84 m of fence among a square's four equal sides

why.en: 84 m of fence shared by four equal sides: 84 ÷ 4 = 21 m

simpler.hi: Square ki bhujayein chaar hain, do nahi, aur sab barabar. Socho, poori baad unmein kaise bategi.

prompt.hi: Ek khet 30 m lamba aur 20 m chauda rectangle hai. Taar ₹15 per metre milti hai. Khet ke chaaron taraf ek baar taar lagane mein kitne rupaye lagenge?

reask.en: How many rupees does wire at ₹15 per metre take once round a field 30 m long and 20 m wide?

did.hi: pehle khet ka parimap joda, phir taar ka kharcha nikala

whyAlt.hi: Aadha chakkar 30 + 20 = 50 m hai, uski taar ₹750 ki; poora chakkar uska do guna, toh ₹1500.

simpler.hi: 30 × 20 khet ki zameen hai, taar nahi. Pehle kinaara nikalo, phir har metre ke ₹15.
simpler.en: 30 × 20 is the field's ground, not wire. Find the edge first, then ₹15 for each metre.

did.hi: 70 cm ki dori se ulta chalkar rectangle ki chaudai nikali
did.en: worked back from a 70 cm string to the rectangle's breadth

viewCaption.hi: Dori mod ke yeh rectangle bana hai: poori dori 70 cm ki, aur ek bhuja par 20 cm likha hai.
viewCaption.en: The string is bent into this rectangle: the whole string is 70 cm, and one side says 20 cm.

why.hi: 70 ka aadha 35 cm, usme se 20 cm lambai gayi, bache 15 cm
why.en: half of 70 is 35 cm; take away the 20 cm length and 15 cm is left

whyShort.hi: 70 ka aadha 35, usme se 20 gaye: 15 cm

whyAlt.hi: Wapas jodke dekho: 20 + 15 + 20 + 15 = 70 cm, toh 15 cm chaudai theek baithti hai.
whyAlt.en: Add it back: 20 + 15 + 20 + 15 = 70 cm, so a 15 cm breadth fits.

simpler.hi: Dori ke chakkar mein lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai do baar. Socho, aadhi dori mein kya-kya aata hai.
simpler.en: In the string's round the length comes twice and the breadth twice. Think what half the string holds.

ladder.why: backward for a square: perimeter 400 m → one side
backward for a rectangle: perimeter and length known → halve, then subtract the length
fencing cost: perimeter × ₹ per metre, then the gate variant → subtract 2 m before multiplying

remediation.move: the round run backward, spoken over the then-card's own board (a pond whose full round is 90 m and length 28 m) and naming none of its numbers: full boundary = 2 lengths + 2 breadths; the opposite corner = half a round = 1 length + 1 breadth → halve first, then take away the length; then the then-card's pond, given by its full round

say.hi: Socho, ek poore chakkar mein har bhuja ek baar aati hai. Rectangle mein do lambai aur do chaudai hoti hain, aur square mein chaar barabar bhujayein. Toh ulta chalte hue, rectangle ka parimap aadha karo aur lambai ghatao; square ka parimap 4 se baanto.
say.en: A full round takes in every side once. A rectangle has two lengths and two breadths, and a square has four equal sides. So going backwards, halve a rectangle’s perimeter and take away the length; share a square’s perimeter by 4.

simpler.hi: Jo chaudai nikle, use wapas jodkar jaancho: lambai, chaudai, lambai aur chaudai milkar poora chakkar banna chahiye.
simpler.en: Check the breadth you find by adding back: length, breadth, length and breadth should make the whole round.

sayAlt.hi: Chhoti sankhya par dekho: parimap 10 cm aur lambai 3 cm. 10 ka aadha 5 cm, yaani ek lambai aur ek chaudai; 5 mein se 3 gaye toh chaudai 2 cm. Jaanch: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.
sayAlt.en: Look at small numbers: perimeter 10 cm and length 3 cm. Half of 10 is 5 cm, one length and one breadth; 5 take away 3 leaves a breadth of 2 cm. Check: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh ek chhota rectangle hai: poora kinaara 10 cm ka, aur ek bhuja 3 cm ki.
viewCaption.en: This is a small rectangle: the whole edge is 10 cm, and one side is 3 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle talaab ke kinaare ek poora chakkar 90 m ka hai. Talaab 28 m lamba hai. Woh kitna chauda hai?
prompt.en: One full round of the edge of a rectangular pond is 90 m. The pond is 28 m long. How wide is it?

reask.hi: Jis 28 m lambe talaab ka poora chakkar 90 m hai, woh kitna chauda hai?
reask.en: A pond 28 m long is 90 m all the way round; how wide is it?

viewCaption.hi: Talaab ki ek bhuja par 28 m likha hai, aur poore chakkar par 90 m.
viewCaption.en: One side of the pond says 28 m, and the full round says 90 m.

why.hi: 90 ka aadha 45 m, usme se 28 m lambai gayi, bache 17 m
why.en: half of 90 is 45 m; take away the 28 m length and 17 m is left

whyShort.hi: 90 ka aadha 45, usme se 28 gaye: 17 m

whyAlt.hi: Do lambai milke 56 m; 90 mein se 56 gaye toh do chaudai ke liye 34 m bache, aur ek chaudai 17 m.
whyAlt.en: Two lengths make 56 m; 90 take away 56 leaves 34 m for the two breadths, and one breadth is 17 m.

simpler.hi: Poore chakkar mein do lambai aur do chaudai hain. Socho, aadhe chakkar mein kya aata hai, aur usmein se lambai nikal kar kya bachega.
simpler.en: A whole round has two lengths and two breadths. Think what half a round holds, and what is left when the length is taken out.

remediation.move: wire is bought by the metre of edge, not by the ground inside: thread around the plot vs tiles inside it; cost = edge length (m) × ₹ per m; l × b = ground covered, not wire

say.hi: Socho, ek plot ke chaaron taraf taar lag rahi hai. Lambai aur chaudai ka guna andar ki zameen hai, taar nahi. Taar kinaare par lagti hai, toh pehle kinaare ki poori lambai nikalo, phir har metre ke daam se guna karo.
say.en: Length times breadth is the ground inside, not the wire. Wire goes on the edge, so find the edge's full length first, then multiply by the price per metre.

simpler.hi: Socho taar kahan lagegi: plot ke beech mein ya uske kinaare par. Jahan lagegi, paise sirf wahi metre lete hain.
simpler.en: Think where the wire goes: across the middle of the plot or round its edge. Only the metres where it goes cost money.

sayAlt.hi: Dukaan par taar kapde ki tarah metre ke hisaab se bikti hai. Dukaandaar poochega kitne metre chahiye, zameen kitni badi hai yeh nahi; toh pehle kinaare ke metre jodo, phir har metre ka daam lagao.
sayAlt.en: At the shop wire is sold by the metre, like cloth. The shopkeeper asks how many metres you need, not how big the ground is; so add up the metres of edge first, then put the price on each metre.

prompt.hi: {friendM} ne 9 m lambe, 6 m chaude plot par ₹20 per metre wali taar ka kharcha ₹1080 bataya. Sahi kharcha kitna hai?
prompt.en: {friendM} said wire at ₹20 a metre round a plot 9 m long and 6 m wide costs ₹1080. What is the right cost?

reask.hi: Jis plot ki bhujayein 9 m, 6 m, 9 m aur 6 m hain, uske kinaare par ₹20 per metre ki taar lagane mein sahi kitne rupaye lagenge?
reask.en: A plot has sides 9 m, 6 m, 9 m and 6 m; how many rupees does it really take to put wire at ₹20 per metre along its edge?

viewCaption.hi: Plot ki chaaron bhujayein ek line mein hain: 9 m, 6 m, 9 m, 6 m. Taar sirf isi line par lagti hai, andar ki zameen par nahi.
viewCaption.en: The plot's four sides are in one line: 9 m, 6 m, 9 m, 6 m. Wire goes only along this line, not on the ground inside.

whyAlt.hi: Har metre ₹20 ka, aur kinaara 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m, toh 30 baar ₹20, yaani ₹600; 9 × 6 = 54 toh zameen thi.
whyAlt.en: Each metre is ₹20, and the edge is 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m, so ₹20 thirty times, which is ₹600; 9 × 6 = 54 was the ground.

simpler.hi: 9 × 6 zameen hai, taar nahi. Pehle plot ka kinaara nikalo, phir har metre ke ₹20.
simpler.en: 9 × 6 is the ground, not the wire. First find the plot's edge, then ₹20 for each metre.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein parimap se kaam liya: square ki bhuja, rectangle ki chaudai, chakkaron ki doori aur taar ka kharcha nikala.
covered.en: Last we put perimeter to work: a square's side, a rectangle's breadth, the distance of rounds, the cost of wire.

prompt.hi: Ek seedhe taar ko mod ke 27 cm lamba aur 9 cm chauda rectangle banana hai, bina kuch bachaaye. Taar kitne centimetre lambi honi chahiye?
prompt.en: A straight wire is bent into a rectangle 27 cm long and 9 cm wide, with none left over. How many centimetres long must the wire be?

did.hi: 27 cm aur 9 cm wale rectangle ki taar ki lambai nikali
did.en: found the wire length for a 27 cm by 9 cm rectangle

why.hi: Taar sirf kinaare par mudti hai: aadha chakkar 27 + 9 = 36 cm, aur poora chakkar 2 × 36 = 72 cm.
why.en: The wire only bends along the edge: half a round is 27 + 9 = 36 cm, and the full round 2 × 36 = 72 cm.

simpler.hi: Taar chaaron bhujaon par mudti hai: dono lambai aur dono chaudai.
simpler.en: The wire bends along all four sides: both lengths and both breadths.

viewCaption.en: Straighten the wire back out and it looks like this: 27 cm, 9 cm, 27 cm, 9 cm, one after another.

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki parimap band shape ke poore kinaare ki lambai hai, jismein har bhuja ek baar judti hai. Rectangle ka parimap 2 × (lambai + chaudai), square ka 4 × bhuja, aur parimap se ulta bhuja nikalti hai.
covered.en: Today we saw that perimeter is a closed shape's whole edge, with every side added once. A rectangle's perimeter is 2 × (length + breadth), a square's 4 × side, and a side can be found back from it.
